hypothesis: opzsim.call silently spins when step() refuses an instruction
test: Make call() compare m.steps around step() and raise naming the pc and halfword when nothing executed, and drop the duplicated dead 'if lenient' block
notes: the guard was added in toolkit/opzsim.py and the selftest still reports all checks passed over 519,370 steps, so a hung run now reports the instruction instead of spending the whole budget and blaming the callee - it was the reason several earlier probes had to be killed by hand

hypothesis: The OS per-voice tick's remaining blocker is the chip's on-chip L2 ROM, not missing OS memory
test: Run the OS note-start (0x8012E0A4) and then the tick (0x8012E2C0) for analoga, ministringshort and saw013a in the whole-address-space machine, with call() refusing any pc that no LDR segment covers
notes: all three now reach the tick and stop in exactly the same place after 68 steps: an absolute CALL.A at 0x8011aa8c whose 32-bit target is 0x04020a70. Nothing in either LDR image maps the 0x04 region - opz.ldr's 164 segments cover only 0x11A (L1), 0x08 (L2 SRAM) and 0x80 (main image) - while the ADSP-BF70x datasheet lists a 512 kB on-chip L2 ROM, so 0x04020a70 is mask ROM that no shipped artifact contains

hypothesis: Only a handful of ROM entry points stand between the OS tick and audio
test: Scan the loaded image for Jump32 absolute CALL/JUMP opcodes (halfword 0xDE00) whose target lands in 0x04000000-0x0403FFFF
notes: the scan finds 1,195 such call sites naming 51 distinct ROM entry points, with 0x04022ea8 called from 249 sites and 0x04020a70 from 16, so the ROM is woven through the OS rather than touched once - emulating it is a porting programme of 51 routines against undocumented mask-ROM semantics, not a harness fix

hypothesis: Analoga, fm003b, ministringshort and saw013a fault in the engine-only machine and not in the OS one
test: Compare their render in Machine.for_module (flat window, OS calls return 0) with the OS-driven voice path (opzos.build: full 4 GB sparse machine, engine at its own load base, OS note-start and tick)
notes: engine-only they leave the module window or call a null pointer after 18k-34k steps, but in the OS machine they finish init and note-start cleanly (analoga 719 steps, ministringshort 1,210, saw013a 771) and only the tick stops, at the ROM call above - so their engine-only faults were harness artifacts and the real blocker is shared with the samplers

hypothesis: opzsim's call() needs three guards the whole-address-space machine exposed
test: Fix and re-run the interpreter selftest
notes: (1) RETS 0 was treated as a usable return address because _off(0) is inside the window arithmetically, which ping-ponged forever - found as a 4096-count null-call loop; (2) calls through a zero word cost no step, so the step ceiling never fired and the loop never ended, now capped by NULL_CALL_LIMIT; (3) with check_coverage set, a jump to an address no LDR segment covers now raises naming the address instead of marching through 200,000 NOP steps. selftest: 519,370 steps, 0 failures

hypothesis: Mapping the OS image is enough to keep analoga, fm003b, ministringshort and saw013a alive on their own render
test: Call each engine's render export directly in the whole-address-space machine (opzos.build, host table installed at 0x81003850, six-stack-word convention) instead of going through the per-voice tick
notes: they fail exactly as they did in the engine-only machine: fm003b 'null function pointer' after 27,881 steps, saw013a 'execution at 0xf757a802' after 18,583, ministringshort 'call did not return' at 200,000. Having the firmware's memory present changes nothing, so these engines need the OS tick to build their context - and the tick needs the chip's ROM, which makes them blocked on the same thing rather than on the memory map

hypothesis: Organ renders audio once the firmware's sine table is present, not just a numerical whisper
test: Force its R2 gate at 0x81b7d1c4 inside the whole-address-space machine, where 0x0800bb48 holds the real quarter-sine, and render six blocks
notes: its peak goes from 1 of 2^31 (engine-only, table zeroed) to 3,291,556 - a real burst, 51 of 64 samples nonzero - but only in block 1, with blocks 0 and 2-5 silent, so the remaining gap is organ's own state rather than the table. Its ctx block is written identically during every block (73 stores, ctx+0x04/0x10/0x20/0x24/0x30/0x34 leading), so the silence is not a field the render stops updating

hypothesis: Organ's remaining silence is a memory fill away
test: With the OS machine's real sine table present and the R2 gate forced at 0x81b7d1c4, fill its dense zero-read region 0x81bbfe00-0x81bc0000 with 0x40000000, 0x7fff7fff and 0x10000 and render five identical blocks
notes: all three fills give the identical result to no fill at all - nonzero samples per block 0/51/0/0/1 with peak 3,291,556 in block 1 only - while every block executes the full 18,601-step body. So organ reaches its DSP and writes zeros from its own arithmetic or state, and the zero-read region is not what feeds its output. Also confirmed by step trace that R2 at the gate is loaded from [FP+0x40] by 0xa10a at 0x81b7d1c2, i.e. an unwritten frame slot, so forcing it stands in for stack residue rather than for engine data

hypothesis: Organ reads its caller's unwritten stack, so its remaining output depends on OS residue
test: Make opzsim.call restore SP after the call (the caller owns the argument words) so successive renders no longer walk the frame down 24 bytes each, then re-render six blocks with the R2 gate forced
notes: before the fix the frame drifted 24 bytes per render and organ's output was one block in five (0/51/0/0/1 of 64). After it the pattern becomes 0/0/1/1/1/0 with peaks up to 11,847,907, i.e. single-sample impulses that move as the residue changes. The diff of reads between a loud block and a silent one is dominated by stack words 0x81feffd0-0x81feffdc and the gate input itself is R2 = [FP+0x40], an unwritten frame slot, so organ's amplitude and phase come from stack residue the OS tick leaves - which sits behind the same ROM call. Selftest still 519,370 steps / 0 failures and the tallies are unchanged: 13 of 13 instruments, 7 of 8 effects, chord+digital on the strict Blackfin check

hypothesis: The chip's L2 ROM can be identified and emulated from Analog Devices' documentation
test: Check the ADSP-BF70x Hardware Reference for an address-indexed ROM function table that would name 0x04020a70
notes: the manual's Table 11-1 'L2 Memory Address Mapping' confirms the region exactly - '0x04000000 0x407FFFFF L2 Bank 0 ROM (512 KB)' - and the boot chapter names routines such as adi_rom_Boot() and adi_rom_MemCopy(), but there is no address-indexed table and no entry near 0x04020a70. So the ROM's contents are unpublished mask ROM: the OS's 1,195 calls into 51 entries cannot be emulated faithfully from documentation, which closes the Blackfin tick path as a documented dead end rather than an unfinished probe

hypothesis: Saw013a leaves the module by jumping through bad data
test: Track every write to RETS during a render and check whether the harness stack window is being overwritten by engine frames
notes: it is not an indirect jump: the engine completes its whole 18,929-step body and its standard epilogue (0x6ca6, 0x05a3, 0xe801, 0x0010), and RETS changes only five times. The last change is the UNLINK at 0x81b78ba6 restoring 0xf757a802 - a constant the module carries three times - while the sibling frame slot holds 0x66666666, so the engine's own frame was overwritten during the body. Moving the harness stack from 0x81ff0000 to 0x8ff00000 changes nothing (and fm003b, ministringshort and analoga fail identically), so this is engine or host-service behaviour, not a stack-window collision: the four engines get essentially to the end of render and lose their frame

hypothesis: The 6-of-13 audible Blackfin tally can be reproduced without the ad-hoc probes it was measured with
test: Add toolkit/opzfactoryaudible.py, which renders every factory instrument through render_clip with each engine's documented prerequisite (cluster R3 gate, electric coefficient table, organ R2 gate) and applies a stated floor: at least 1% of samples nonzero and a peak of 1e-4 of full scale
notes: one command now reports 6 of 13, matching the recorded tally exactly: AUDIBLE chord 879/1920 at 0.0625, cluster 487/1920 at 0.0002 (with its gate), digital 1777/1920 at 0.124, electric 1920/1920 at 0.6692 (with its table), ep 959/1920 at 0.0211, volt 1152/1920 at 1.0; silent fm003b, organ (27/1920 at 1/2^31, i.e. the transient), sampleplayergain, saw013a, synthsampler; ERROR analoga and ministringshort with 'engine keeps calling outside its window'. opzinstcheck still 13 of 13, opzfxcheck 7 of 8, opzfactorycheck 2 of 13, and the interpreter selftest is green over 519,370 steps

hypothesis: Analoga and ministringshort fail because the harness hands them no buffer from the OS
test: Retry them with opzsim's bump allocator enabled (host_bump at 0x82000000, step 0x10000) so every out-of-window call returns a fresh address instead of 0
notes: identical failure with and without the bump allocator - both raise 'engine keeps calling outside its window' - and the underlying fault is not a missing buffer: the outside fetch is pc = RETS = 0xeb9670e6, a garbage address, hit 65 times in a row. Tracing the frame shows the SP bookkeeping is balanced (inner LINK at 0x81b93918 takes SP 0x81bd5ee8 to 0x81bd5de8, and the matching UNLINK at 0x81b93a22 runs at 0x81bd5de0), but the frame slot holds 0x81bd5ee0 - a stack address - where the saved RETS belongs, and the outermost UNLINK at 0x81b94324 pops RETS 0 and FP 0xe459dfe5. So engine code clobbers its own saved return slot, which is the same pathology as saw013a's 0xf757a802 and is not a harness allocation problem

hypothesis: The device-side effect modules were never part of the engine tally
test: List engines-official and run every module through opzfactoryaudible.py, which now measures both kinds: 13 instruments and 8 effects
notes: the eight factory effect .engine modules (chorus, chorus2, crush, delay, dist, fdnreverb, reverb, tapetwo) had no entry in any tally - only the vendor ARM64 library covered effects. Measured with the toolkit's current renderFX convention: chorus, chorus2, crush, delay and dist run but write zero output (0/1920), while fdnreverb and tapetwo stop on 'null function pointer' and reverb on 'keeps calling outside its window'. So the device-side population is 6 of 13 instruments and 0 of 8 effects, and the audit checklist now covers all 21 shipped .engine modules

hypothesis: render_clip's five-argument renderFX convention is right for the factory effect .engine modules
test: Compare it with the six-argument vendor signature renderFX(params, frames, state, in, out, scratch) that opzfxcheck drives
notes: the .engine effects are called with (ctx, freq, state) in registers and (inp, out) on the stack, which is one argument short of the vendor signature, so their all-zero output is not yet evidence that the engines are silent - it may be a calling-convention mismatch. This is the next thing to establish before the 0 of 8 figure is quoted as an engine result

hypothesis: One of the plausible renderFX argument orders makes the factory effect .engine modules write into the output buffer
test: Sweep six conventions on dist.engine - (ctx,frames,state)+(in,out), (out,frames,state)+(in,ctx), (out,frames,ctx)+(in,state), (out,frames)+(in,state,ctx), (out,frames,state)+(in,ctx,prm) and (ctx,out,in)+(frames,state) - counting writes into the out page
notes: not one of the six writes a single word into the output buffer: every variant leaves out at 0/128 nonzero and instead stores about 1040 words into the zero page. Setting ctx+0=out and ctx+4=in, or the reverse, or adding ctx+8=1024, changes nothing either. So the effect modules do not take their output pointer from the call arguments at all, and the 0 of 8 effect figure measures a harness mismatch rather than silent engines

hypothesis: How dist.engine reaches its output
test: Locate the zero-page stores and the ctx reads during renderFX
notes: its only ctx reads are ctx+0 and ctx+4, once each, at 0x81bfa108 and 0x81bfa110, and both are zero. It stores 5 times each to addresses 0x04, 0x08, 0x0c ... through a base pointer of zero at pc 0x81bfa4b2 (P0 ends at 0 while P1/P2 hold 0x200/0x208), and writes its own data page 0x81c3a000. That is the same OS-populated-state signature as the instruments: the buffer pointers the engine walks are fields the OS fills before a block, not arguments

hypothesis: TapeTwo is silent because the host never performs the sampleLine -> tapeBuffer_z transfer
test: Answer the interface, verify sampleLine holds the input, and then perform that copy from the host at the engine's own transfer service call (svc1 with opcode 0xa0002), 4 copies per block over 8 blocks
notes: the copy runs 32 times and the output is still 0 of 1024. The premise is also wrong: with every interface slot stubbed to return 1, sampleLine_l is filled with the input (16 of 16 nonzero words, first 61800448), and a read/write timeline over one block shows renderFX itself writing 128 zero words into tapeBuffer_l - interleaved offsets 0, 128, 2, 130 ... - and then reading those same 128 back. So the engine zeroes and re-reads the tape buffer inside the block, after its host calls, and the handover's 'missing host conversion' explanation does not hold

hypothesis: TapeTwo's sixth argument is the tape read buffer
test: Fill the scratch argument with the input sine before each renderFX and count output
notes: output stays 0 of 768 with the scratch buffer filled and empty, so silence is not the sixth argument either. Per block renderFX issues six host calls - slot 0 with opcode 1, slot 1 with opcode 5, slot 0 with opcode 0, slot 1 with opcode 6 and slot 1 twice with opcode 0xa0002 - and returns 1-answers for all of them do not change the result, which narrows what is left to the tape buffer's own mix path

hypothesis: The factory effect .engine modules expose their scratch buffer as a module global the host fills
test: Read dist.engine's null pointer: it loads 0x81bfa554 (=0 after init) as P0 and stores through it; set that word to a real buffer before renderFX and count the null-area stores
notes: init itself clears it - two stores at 0x81bfa0e2/0x81bfa0e4 write 0x200 to module+0x558 and 0x0 to module+0x554, and no init argument changes that, so the host is expected to fill it before each block. Supplying a buffer there drops the null-area stores from 1040 to 270, which confirms the field is a scratch pointer, but the output buffer is still untouched and 270 stores still go to low addresses (pcs 0x81bfa1a4, 0x81bfa1b8, 0x81bfa1ca write to 4, 8, 0x204 with P3 = 0x81128264), so the effect also takes its output base from OS state and no convention among the ones tried supplies it

hypothesis: Rendering audio and playing the requested note are the same thing for the vendor ARM64 instruments
test: Add a dominant-bin measurement to opzinstcheck (tail window, mean removed, Hann, 80-3000 Hz scan with a fine pass) and read it against the requested note 60 = 261.6 Hz
notes: all 13 render audio between 2556 and 2560 nonzero samples, but only Digital lands within a semitone of the requested note (267.5 Hz, +38 cents). EP and MiniStringShort sit on the second harmonic (+32 and +134 cents), Organ on the fourth (+147), and AnalogA, Chord, Fm003b, Saw013a and Volt put their dominant energy near 140-150 Hz, about half the request, while Cluster, SamplePlayerGain and SynthSampler peak at 75 Hz. So '13 of 13 render audio' was accurate as stated but must not be read as '13 of 13 play the note', and the column is labelled informational because a dominant-bin scan is not a pitch tracker on a multi-partial engine

hypothesis: The vendor ARM64 instruments that miss the dominant bin also fail to play the requested note
test: Add --note-check to opzinstcheck: render 140 blocks (8192 samples per channel) and compare the requested note's spectral energy with its 0.75x and 1.5x neighbours, the same test opzfactorycheck applies to the Blackfin side
notes: 7 of 13 beat both neighbours at the current convention - Digital 11.71 (neighbours 0.74/1.19), EP 7.90 (0.71/0.69), Electric 25.05 (1.24/0.83), MiniStringShort 33.41 (1.18/5.10), Saw013a 26.57 (3.11/1.88), SynthSampler 153.60 (47.01/64.12) and Volt 16.32 (5.23/0.84) - while AnalogA 0.66 (1.53/0.69), Cluster 27.49 (52.00/12.21), SamplePlayerGain 27.81 (52.60/12.33) and Organ 0.17 (2.32/1.36) lose to a neighbour and Chord 84.29 loses to its own fourth (1404.87) and Fm003b 9.30 to 154.62. So the strongest partial is not the note, the dominant-bin column was misleading, and the six failures cluster where the engine is either interval-based or still needs its pitch-argument scale calibrated - not proof that those engines cannot play

hypothesis: The six vendor instruments that lost the neighbour test all need the same pitch scale
test: Sweep the render's phase increment over 0.25x-4x for each, then re-check the winner with the full 140-block neighbour test
notes: only Chord and Fm003b needed a different scale, and it is the same factor of two the Blackfin path documents as a half-size table: Fm003b goes from 9.30 (neighbours 154.62/62.10) at x1 to 6133.99 (29.91/17.37) at x2, and Chord from 84.29 (loses to its own fourth, 1404.87) to 32388.86 (167.17/97.67) at x1.7 and 34504.93 at x2. Recording both as PHASE_SCALE in opzinstcheck lifts the note tally from 7 to 9 of 13. AnalogA stays at request 0.66-1.00 for every scale up to x2 and Organ at 0.17-0.63 up to x3, so those two do not play the request at all; Cluster and SamplePlayerGain are scale-independent at 27.49 and 27.81, which is what a fixed-sample engine looks like and means the neighbour test is not meaningful for them

hypothesis: AnalogA and Organ only need a per-engine phase scale like Chord and Fm003b
test: Search for the scale that maximises the request contrast and then check it tracks across notes 48, 60 and 72, with Digital at x1 as the control
notes: both engines can be made to pass at one note, but neither yields a defensible scale. AnalogA passes at x1.84 (34.93 against 1.46/0.68) and repeats at all three notes (30.7/34.0/32.3), yet 1.84 is not a clean table ratio and x2.0 falls straight back to 1.00. Organ passes at x0.25 (51.22 against 0.98/1.92) and x0.5 (38.90) but only holds across notes at 48 and 60 (245.4/55.2) and collapses at 72 (1.7). The control settles it: Digital at x1, which is a known-good scale, fails the same three-note test at note 72 (1.4 against 1.2/1.6), so the multi-note contrast test is not yet decisive and adding 1.84 or 0.25 would fit the harness to the metric rather than to the engine

hypothesis: An f0 tracker will settle AnalogA, Cluster, Organ and SamplePlayerGain
test: Implement harmonic product spectrum, then a whitened harmonic-sum search with 1-cent grid over 60-1200 Hz, and validate against Digital, whose scale is certainly right
notes: neither tracker is usable yet. HPS reports Digital at 427.7 Hz for a 261.6 Hz request (+851 cents) and 70.5 Hz at note 48, and the whitened harmonic-sum reports Digital at 143.5 Hz for the 261.6 Hz request (-1039 cents) - an octave below - then the same octave-down answer for AnalogA at all three notes. The cause is structural, not a tuning detail: a harmonic series anchored at f/2 contains every harmonic of f, so the sum scores as well or better at half the true f0 unless subharmonics are penalised. Contrast stays the only metric that behaves, which is why the remaining four stay unjudged rather than being scored by a tracker with a known octave error

hypothesis: A single note is enough to say whether an engine plays the requested pitch
test: Add --note to opzinstcheck and run the 140-block neighbour test at notes 57, 60 and 72 for all 13 vendor instruments
notes: the answer is note-dependent, so one note is not enough. Six engines beat both neighbours at all three notes - Chord (60992/34504/517), EP (6.66/7.90/2.58), Electric (25.04/25.05/4.23), Fm003b (7910/6133/170), MiniStringShort (272.99/33.41/4.29) and Saw013a (49.81/26.57/2.13) - while Digital passes 57 and 60 but fails 72 (1.37 against 1.15/1.53), Organ passes only 57 (109.98 against 0.12/9.81), SynthSampler only 60 (153.60) and losing at 57 to 381.63, and AnalogA, Cluster and SamplePlayerGain fail at every note (AnalogA 1.49/0.66/0.67; Cluster 38.89/27.49/6.87 each losing to its 0.75x neighbour; SamplePlayerGain 39.33/27.81/6.95 likewise). It also corrects the previous round's reading: Digital failing at note 72 is engine behaviour, not a defect in the test

hypothesis: The render's phase increment is the one the clone's phase_increment() returns
test: Compute the increment directly as Q32 at the 48 kHz read rate - inc = freq/48000 * 2**32 - and re-run the 140-block neighbour test at notes 57, 60 and 72
notes: the clone returns Q31 for 44.1 kHz (freq/44100 * 2**31 = 12740059 for note 60), which is 1/2.177 of what a 32-bit accumulator at 48 kHz needs, and the engines read it exactly that way: Digital's measured fundamental was 140.6 Hz for a 261.6 Hz request, and 12740059/2**32 * 48000 = 142.4 Hz. Supplying the Q32 value lifts the note-60 tally from 9 to 11 of 13 and gives 9 engines that pass at all three notes (AnalogA, Chord, Digital, EP, Electric, Fm003b, MiniStringShort, Saw013a, Volt). It also shows the earlier Chord/Fm003b x2 'half-size table' scale was really this unit error, so PHASE_SCALE is now empty except for EP and Electric, which do take the old Q31-at-44.1-kHz unit (scale 0.5442: EP 8.86 against 0.65/0.60, Electric 20.61 against 1.09/1.41)

hypothesis: Cluster and SamplePlayerGain fail every note because their sample record is wrong
test: Give the samplers a sample recorded at the root pitch (a 261.63 Hz sine, note 60 at 48 kHz) and declare that pitch in the record's +0x0c field in the same Q32 unit the render argument uses, instead of a period-64 table declared at the old Q31-at-44.1-kHz value
notes: the record change does reach the engines - SamplePlayerGain's peak rises from 28,114,945 to 1,767,964,668 and SynthSampler's from 1,201,894,485 to 1,553,395,630 and it keeps its note-60 pass at 282.61 - but both samplers now produce the same output at notes 57, 60 and 72 (Cluster 848,755,646 and SamplePlayerGain 1,767,964,668 at every note) with contrasts identical to two decimals (38.89/27.50/6.87 against 38.89/27.49/6.87). So their playback rate does not track the render increment at all in this harness and comes from somewhere else, and the neighbour test, which assumes a pitched oscillator, is not a meaningful instrument for them: they stay out of the tally rather than being called silent

hypothesis: The samplers' playback rate lives in the sample record's +0x10 field
test: Expose the record pointer from supply() as so.rec, vary +0x10 over 2^12, 2^16, 2^20 and 2^24 for SamplePlayerGain and Cluster, and measure the dominant frequency at note 60
notes: no field value changes anything: both engines report the same dominant figure (75.0 Hz, which is the low end of the pitch() scan, i.e. envelope energy rather than a note) at all four settings, and the neighbour contrast is likewise unchanged. So the playback rate is not the record's +0x10 field. Both samplers also return identical dominant figures to each other whatever the class, note or record contents, while their peaks differ (848,755,646 for Cluster against 1,767,964,668 for SamplePlayerGain), so they stay out of the tally until the rate field is found - the next step is to trace which state word onNoteOn writes for these two

hypothesis: The samplers learn the note from onNoteOn or from render's third argument
test: Snapshot the whole 1 KB state block after onNoteOn at notes 60 and 72 and diff it, then re-render with render's third argument set to the note
notes: onNoteOn writes nothing note-dependent at all: the state block after note 60 and after note 72 is byte-identical for both SamplePlayerGain and Cluster (0 differing words out of 256). Passing the note as render's third argument changes nothing either - the request contrast and neighbours stay the same to one decimal (SamplePlayerGain 37.5 against 71.0/16.7 at note 60 both ways, 9.4 against 16.7/4.1 at note 72). So neither the note-on argument nor the render arguments nor the sample record reach the samplers' playback rate, and their output is note-invariant; judging them needs a per-engine read of SamplePlayerGain::render rather than another harness-side guess

hypothesis: The samplers' 117 Hz output is the supplied sample played at a fixed rate
test: Change the recorded sample's own frequency to 130.81 Hz and 523.25 Hz (and leave it at 261.63) and measure the dominant output of SamplePlayerGain
notes: the output is 117.2 Hz for all three sample frequencies, and also for params[0]=0, 0x08000000, 0x10000000, params[1] and params[2] at 0x20000000, and for record+0x0c at 12740059 or 23406890 (only 1<<24 and 1<<28 silence it). Cluster returns the identical 117.2 Hz throughout. So the audible component is engine-internal rather than sample playback: the record is demonstrably read - its pitch unit change earlier moved SamplePlayerGain's peak from 28,114,945 to 1,767,964,668 and 'params all zero' silences both - but nothing the harness can set moves the 117 Hz component, so these two are not playing the sample at all in this harness and cannot be judged by the note test

hypothesis: SamplePlayerGain never touches the sample record during render
test: Hook memory reads inside the record (0x28 bytes) and inside the 8192-frame sample buffer while rendering four blocks at note 60
notes: it reads both. Per block it reads record+0x0c (the pitch field) once and record+0x10 (the rate field) once, and it reads 256 words from the sample buffer - two per frame - all of them in the last quarter of the buffer (byte offsets 7168-8191). So the record and the sample are both consumed every block, which means the 117 Hz figure is not evidence that the sampler ignores its input; it is evidence that the measurement is misreading the output (the two-per-frame reads advance the position slowly enough that a 60-block run never leaves that quarter). Judging these two needs the actual read of render's mix loop rather than another black-box frequency estimate

hypothesis: SamplePlayerGain's output is invariant because its measurement is wrong, not because its position is stuck
test: Log the sample frame positions it reads in each of ten consecutive blocks at note 60
notes: the position IS stuck: every block makes 256 sample reads - two per frame - at exactly frames 2038, 2039 and 2040, an advance of 2 frames over 64 frames of output, and the same three frames in all ten blocks. So the engine replays a two-frame fragment and its output is essentially constant, which is exactly why every frequency estimate came back at the same 117 Hz and why no note or field changed it. The previous round's correction stands - the record and sample are read every block - but the earlier 'measurement artefact' explanation is replaced by this: the playback position never advances. What the harness is missing is whatever advances it, and that is engine state, not a host field among the ones tested
